1. (Currently Amended) A computer-implemented method comprising:determining, by a computing system, detection data associated with an environment;
determining, by the computing system, map data associated with the environment,
wherein the map data includes information associated with a presence of an emergency lane that is different from a rescue lane;determining, by the computing system, a rescue lane scenario associated with the environment based on the map data and satisfaction of rescue lane conditions associated with the rescue lane scenario by the detection data; and
generating, by the computing system, planning and control data for a vehicle based on the rescue lane scenario.
2. (Original) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, wherein the detection data includes information associated with at least one of detected vehicles, detected construction signs, detected lane markings, detected road boundaries, distances between the vehicle and detected obstacles, speeds of detected obstacles, and directions of detected obstacles.
3. (Currently Amended) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, further comprising:
determining, by the computing system, map data associated with the environment, wherein the map data further includes information associated with at least one of a type of road; and a number of lanes, and a presence of an emergency lane, and wherein the determining the rescue lane scenario associated with the environment is based on the map data.
4. (Original) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, wherein the rescue lane conditions include at least one of a condition satisfied by a road that includes at least two lanes in a direction of the vehicle, a condition satisfied by a road that lacks an emergency lane or a shoulder lane, a condition satisfied by a speed of vehicles in a lane of the vehicle below a threshold speed, a condition satisfied by a speed of vehicles in an adjacent lane to a lane of the
vehicle below a threshold speed, and a condition satisfied by lateral biasing of vehicles in a lane of the vehicle.
5. (Original) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, wherein determining the rescue lane scenario associated with the environment comprises:determining, by the computing system, the vehicle is in a leftmost lane of a road or the vehicle is in a rightmost lane of the road; and
determining, by the computing system, vehicles in the leftmost lane of the road are laterally biased to a left of the leftmost lane or the vehicles in the rightmost lane of the road are laterally biased to a right of the rightmost lane.
6. (Original) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, wherein generating the planning and control data for the vehicle comprises:generating, by the computing system, an alert for a driver of the vehicle;
determining, by the computing system, an amount of lateral bias;
causing, by the computing system, the vehicle to laterally bias based on the amount of lateral bias; and
causing, by the computing system, the vehicle to maintain speed based on a leading vehicle in front of the vehicle.
7. (Original) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, wherein generating the planning and control data for the vehicle comprises:identifying, by the computing system, an opportunity to make a lane change; and
causing, by the computing system, the vehicle to refrain from making the lane change.
8. (Original) The computer-implemented method of claim 1, further comprising:determining, by the computing system, an end of the rescue lane scenario based on satisfaction of rescue lane end conditions, wherein the rescue lane end conditions include at least one of a condition satisfied by a speed of vehicles in a lane of the vehicle over a threshold speed, a condition satisfied by a speed of vehicles in an adjacent lane to a lane of the vehicle over a threshold speed, and a condition satisfied by centering of vehicles in a lane of the vehicle.
9. (Original) The computer-implemented method of claim 8, further comprising:generating, by the computing system, an alert for a driver of the vehicle;
causing, by the computing system, the vehicle to center to a middle of a lane of the vehicle; and
causing, by the computing system, the vehicle to increase speed based on vehicles in the lane of the vehicle.
10. (Original) The computer-implemented method of claim 8, further comprising:identifying, by the computing system, an opportunity to make a lane change; and
causing, by the computing system, the vehicle to make the lane change based on the end of the rescue lane scenario.
